# Volume 2 — X Robin in Search of a Sensation

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

As Nell journeyed back from school along the Aspen Path on a November afternoon, she experienced a renewed certainty that living was a truly marvelous affair. Her day had proven to be a pleasant one, with everything running smoothly within her small realm. St. Clair Trask had refrained from brawling with any of his male peers regarding his name; Prillie Rogerson’s face was so swollen as a result of a toothache that she refrained from attempting even once to flirt with the nearby boys. Barbara Shaw had suffered merely a single mishap . . . slopping a water dipper across the floor . . . and Anthony Tulk had been entirely absent from class.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0000 }

“This November has been such a pleasant month!” remarked Nell, whose childhood tendency to speak aloud to herself had never completely vanished. “Usually, November is a most unpleasant period . . . as though the year abruptly realized her advancing age and could only cry and complain about it. However, this year is aging with elegance . . . much like an elegant elderly woman who understands her ability to remain delightful despite her grey hair and lines. Lovely days and delightful dusks have been ours. A profound sense of peace has marked these past two weeks, and Robin himself has been nearly well-mannered. Truly, I believe his behavior is getting much better. The forest is so silent today . . . lacking any sound save for the gentle breeze whispering among the highest branches! That noise resembles ocean waves breaking on a distant coast. These woods are so precious! My splendid trees! Each single one of you is beloved by me as a friend.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0001 }

Stopping briefly, Nell wrapped her arm around a slender young birch tree to press a kiss against its creamy-white bark. Isolde caught sight of her and burst into laughter as she came around a bend in the trail.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0002 }

“Nell Harcourt, you are merely acting as if you are adult. I think that whenever you are by yourself, you are just as much a small girl as you used to be.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0003 }

“Well, a person is unable to abandon the routine of being a small girl immediately,” Nell said cheerfully. “You understand, I remained small for fourteen years and I have been somewhat adult for barely three. I am certain I will constantly feel akin to a youngster in the forest. These journeys home from school represent virtually the sole period I possess for daydreaming . . . with the exception of the thirty minutes or thereabouts prior to sleeping. I am exceedingly occupied with instructing and learning and assisting Thirza regarding the twins that I do not possess a single other instant for picturing things. You are unaware of what grand exploits I experience for a brief duration after retiring to bed in the east gable each evening. I invariably picture that I am an entity exceedingly magnificent and victorious and grand . . . an eminent prima donna or a Red Cross nurse or a monarch. Previous night I was a monarch. It is truly marvelous to picture that you are a monarch. You possess the entire pleasure of it lacking any of the troubles and you are able to cease being a monarch anytime you wish to, which you would be unable to in actual existence. However, here among the trees I prefer to picture entirely varied things . . . I am a dryad residing inside an ancient pine, or a small brown wood-elf concealing myself beneath a wrinkled leaf. That pale birch you discovered me kissing constitutes a sibling of mine. The sole distinction is, she constitutes a tree while I constitute a girl, yet that constitutes no actual distinction. To what place are you traveling, Isolde?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0004 }

“I am going down to the Dicksons, as I promised Alberta that I would assist her with cutting out her new dress. Would you be able to walk down later in the evening, Nell, and accompany me back home?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0005 }

“I might . . . because Gideon Duckett is absent in town,” Nell said, looking somewhat overly guileless.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0006 }

Turning her head with a toss, Isolde reddened and continued walking. Even so, she appeared far from displeased.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0007 }

Nell had every intention of heading over to the Dicksons’ later that day, yet she failed to do so. Upon her arrival at Grey Shutters, she discovered a situation that wiped all other concerns clean from her memory. Thirza came out to the yard to meet her . . . a Thirza whose eyes looked wild.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0008 }

“Nell, Lucy cannot be found!”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0009 }

“Lucy! Missing!” Robin was swinging on the yard gate as Nell gazed at him, and she noticed a playful look in his eyes. “Robin, is her location known to you?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0010 }

“No, I don’t,” Robin said firmly. “Cross my heart, I haven’t seen her since dinner time.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0011 }

“Since one o’clock I have been gone,” Thirza stated. “All at once Thomas Sowerby became ill, so Agatha dispatched a request for my immediate presence. Lucy was in the kitchen playing with her doll and Robin was behind the barn making mud pies when I departed from this place. It was merely thirty minutes ago that I returned home . . . and Lucy was nowhere in sight. Robin insists that he has not laid eyes on her since my departure.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0012 }

“I didn’t either,” Robin declared with gravity.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0013 }

“She has to be nearby,” remarked Nell. “She would not go far off by herself . . . you are aware of how easily frightened she is. Maybe she has drifted off to sleep in a room.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0014 }

Thirza gave a negative movement of her head.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0015 }

“The entire house has been searched by me. However, she might be located in one of the outbuildings.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0016 }

A detailed hunt ensued. The pair of frantic individuals searched through every part of the residence, grounds, and adjacent structures. Searching the fruit groves and the Whispering Wood, Nell shouted for Lucy. Thirza picked up a candle and investigated the basement. Joining both of them one after the other, Robin proved inventive at imagining locations where Lucy might potentially have gone. At last, they gathered once more in the yard.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0017 }

“It is an exceedingly strange matter,” Thirza moaned.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0018 }

“In what place could she be?” Nell asked in misery
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0019 }

“Perhaps she has fallen down the well,” Robin offered with good cheer.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0020 }

Nell and Thirza gazed at one another with dread. Though the same realization had accompanied the two of them during their whole quest, neither had summoned the courage to speak it aloud.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0021 }

“She . . . she might have,” Thirza whispered.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0022 }

Experiencing nausea and dizziness, Nell approached the wellbox and looked inside. Situated on the interior shelf was the bucket. A minuscule glint of stagnant water lay deep beneath. Of all the wells in Brierley, the Abernethy well possessed the greatest depth. Should Lucy. . . yet Nell was unable to confront the thought. Trembling, she turned herself around.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0023 }

“Sprint over to get Mr. Pettifer,” Thirza said, twisting her hands together.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0024 }

“Both Mr. Pettifer and John Henry have gone . . . today they traveled to town. I will retrieve Mr. Pembroke.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0025 }

Mr. Pembroke returned accompanied by Nell, bringing along a length of coiled rope fastened to a clawed tool that used to be the working tip of a grubbing fork. Thirza and Nell remained nearby, freezing and trembling from terror and fear, as Mr. Pembroke searched the well, while Robin, sitting with a leg on each side of the gate, observed the gathered people with an expression showing immense pleasure.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0026 }

At last Mr. Pembroke gave a shake of his head, looking relieved.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0027 }

“Down there is impossible for her to be. Where she might have disappeared to remains a remarkably strange matter, however. Listen, lad, is it certain that you lack any notion of your sister's whereabouts?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0028 }

“I have repeated to you twelve times that I did not,” Robin stated, appearing offended. “Perhaps a vagrant arrived and took her.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0029 }

“Nonsense,” Thirza said sharply, feeling relief from her dreadful terror regarding the well. “Nell, do you think she might have wandered to Mr. Pettifer’s house? Ever since the occasion you brought her there, she has constantly mentioned his parrot.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0030 }

“I find it hard to credit that Lucy would travel so far by herself, yet I will cross over to check,” Nell remarked.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0031 }

No one was watching Robin at that moment, otherwise they would have noticed his expression undergo a most definite transformation. Stepping down silently from the gate, he bolted toward the barn as quickly as his chubby legs were able to bear him.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0032 }

Nell hurried through the meadows toward the Pettifer property, feeling far from optimistic. The residence was secured, the blinds were drawn, and no living creature appeared to be present. Standing upon the porch, she shouted for Lucy in a loud voice.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0033 }

Nutmeg, who was in the kitchen behind her, suddenly shrieked and swore with ferocity; yet amidst his outbursts Nell caught a mournful wail originating from the small structure in the yard that Mr. Pettifer utilized as a toolhouse. Nell rushed over to the door, unfastened the latch, and picked up a tiny human with a tear-streaked face sitting pitifully on an inverted nail keg.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0034 }

“Oh, Lucy, Lucy, you scared us so much! How did you end up in this place?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0035 }

“Robin and I came over to see Nutmeg,” weeping, Lucy said, “however we could not see him in the end, though Robin forced him to swear by kicking against the door. And after that Robin took me to this place and rushed away and closed the door; and I was unable to escape. I wept and wept, I was terrified, and oh, I’m so hungry and cold; and I believed you’d never arrive, Nell.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0036 }

“Robin?” yet Nell was unable to utter anything further. She bore Lucy to her residence with a weighted spirit. The gladness she felt upon discovering the youngster uninjured and secure was overwhelmed by the distress arising from Robin’s conduct. The whim of locking Lucy inside could readily have been forgiven. However, Robin had uttered untruths . . . absolute, heartless untruths regarding the matter. That remained the grim reality, and Nell was unable to ignore it. She felt inclined to sit and weep from pure frustration. She had come to hold Robin in deep affection . . . just how deeply she had failed to realize to this moment . . . and learning that he was responsible for intentional deceit pained her beyond endurance.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0037 }

Thirza heard what Nell had to say without making a sound, an omen of trouble ahead for Robin; Mr. Pembroke chuckled, suggesting a swift punishment for Robin. Once he left for home, Nell comforted and heated the weeping, trembling Lucy, served her meal, and tucked her in. Afterwards, she went back to the kitchen, coinciding with Thirza’s stern entrance as she dragged, or pulled along, the unwilling, cobweb-covered Robin, whom she had only just discovered concealed in the most shadowy nook of the stable.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0038 }

She pulled him down onto the rug in the center of the room, after which she walked over to sit beside the window facing east. In a listless posture, Nell sat by the window facing west. The offender was standing in the space between the two of them. Positioned with his back facing Thirza, it appeared meek, subdued, and frightened; nevertheless, he faced Nell, and despite looking somewhat embarrassed, Robin’s eyes held a glimmer of solidarity, as though he understood he had misbehaved and would suffer the consequences, yet was certain he and Nell would share a chuckle about the whole ordeal afterward.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0039 }

Yet no partially concealed grin met his gaze in the gray eyes of Nell, as could have occurred if mere devilry were involved. Another element was present . . . an aspect both hideous and vile.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0040 }

“In what way could you act in such a manner, Robin?” she inquired mournfully.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0041 }

Robin shifted uneasily.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0042 }

“I only carried it out for amusement. Events have been extraordinarily quiet in this place for such a long time that I believed scaring you people immensely would prove entertaining. Indeed, it turned out to be so.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0043 }

Even though he felt afraid and somewhat repentant, Robin smiled at the memory.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0044 }

“Yet you stated an untruth regarding it, Robin,” Nell said, with an even deeper sense of sorrow.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0045 }

Robin appeared confused.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0046 }

“What is a untruth? Are you referring to a lie?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0047 }

“I am referring to a tale that lacked truth.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0048 }

“Course I did,” Robin admitted openly. “You would not have felt afraid if I hadn’t. It was necessary for me to recount it.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0049 }

The strain of her fear and hard effort was beginning to affect Nell. What completed the effect was the lack of remorse shown by Robin. Her eyes filled up with two large tears.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0050 }

“Oh, Robin, how could you?” she asked, her voice trembling slightly. “Are you not aware of how wrong it was?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0051 }

Robin felt horror-struck. Nell weeping . . . he was the cause of Nell’s tears! A swell of genuine regret swept like a surge over his affectionate small heart and swallowed it up. He hurried to Nell, threw himself onto her lap, wrapped his arms about her neck, and erupted in weeping.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0052 }

“I wasn’t aware that it was bad to tell lies,” he wept. “How was I supposed to understand it was bad? Every one of Mr. Sprott’s children told them constantly each day, and swore on their hearts as well. I reckon Cedric Stanhope never tells lies and I have been attempting extremely hard in this place to be as well-behaved as he is, but now I reckon you will not ever care for me again. However, I feel you could have informed me that it was bad. I am terribly sorry that I have caused you to weep, Nell, and I will not ever tell a lie again.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0053 }

Robin pressed his face against Nell’s shoulder and wept intensely. In an abrupt, joyful surge of insight, Nell embraced him closely while gazing across his curly head toward Thirza.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0054 }

“It wasn’t clear to him that telling lies was incorrect, Thirza. On this occasion, provided he pledges to refrain from uttering untruths in the future, my belief is that we ought to pardon him for that particular aspect.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0055 }

“I shall not do it ever, since I am aware it is wrong,” Robin declared through tears. “Should you catch me uttering another lie at any time, you may . . .” Robin searched in his mind for an appropriate punishment . . . “you may skin me alive, Nell.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0056 }

“Avoid using ‘whopper,’ Robin . . . utilize ‘falsehood’ instead,” the schoolma’am instructed.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0057 }

“Why?” asked Robin, making himself comfortable and gazing upward with a tear-streaked, probing countenance. “Why is whopper not as good as falsehood? I want to know. It is an equally large word.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0058 }

“It is a colloquialism; furthermore, small boys ought not to utilize colloquialisms.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0059 }

“There are a terrible number of actions that one shouldn’t commit,” Robin remarked while sighing. “I had no idea there were that many. I regret that it’s improper to tell whop . . . untruths, because it’s extremely convenient, but because it is bad I won't ever speak another one. How will you punish me for speaking them today? I would like to be told.” Nell turned her gaze pleadingly toward Thirza.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0060 }

“I do not wish to judge the youngster excessively,” Thirza remarked. “It is likely that no one actually informed him that lying was improper, and those Sprott youngsters were hardly suitable associates for him. Unfortunate Mary suffered too much illness to instruct him adequately, and I suppose one cannot anticipate a child of six years to understand such matters naturally. It seems we must simply accept that he lacks all correct knowledge and start from the very start. Nevertheless, a penalty is required for his locking Lucy away, though I am unable to conceive a method other than dispatching him to sleep lacking his evening meal, which we have repeated repeatedly. Are you incapable of proposing an alternative, Nell? It seems to me you should possess that capacity, given the imagination you continuously mention.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0061 }

“However, discipline is terribly disagreeable and I prefer to picture purely delightful scenarios,” stated Nell, hugging Robin. “So many disagreeable matters exist in the world currently that picturing additional ones serves no purpose.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0062 }

Ultimately Robin was dispatched to his room, as per usual, where he was to stay until midday the following morning. Clearly he was engaged in some reflection, because upon Nell going to her own chamber shortly afterward, she detected his soft call of her name. Entering his room, she discovered him upright in bed, knees supporting his elbows and hands holding up his chin.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0063 }

“Nell,” he inquired with gravity, “does everyone do wrong by telling whop . . . untruths? I desire an answer?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0064 }

“Indeed, yes.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0065 }

“For an adult, is it incorrect?”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0066 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0067 }

“In that case,” Robin stated with certainty, “Thirza is wicked, because she informs them. Moreover, she is worse than I am, since I was unaware that it was improper, whereas she is conscious of it.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0068 }

“Robin Farrow, not once in her existence did Thirza share a tale,” Nell declared with indignation.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0069 }

“Indeed she did. On Tuesday last, she informed me that I would suffer a terrible fate if I failed to recite my prayers nightly. Yet I have omitted them for more than seven days, merely to test the outcome . . . and absolutely nothing occurred,” Robin stated, sounding quite offended.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0070 }

Suppressing a wild urge to burst into laughter out of the belief that doing so would prove disastrous, Nell subsequently applied herself with all seriousness to preserving the good name of Thirza.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0071 }

“Well, Robin Farrow,” she declared gravely, “a terrible event has occurred to you on this exact day.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0072 }

Robin appeared doubtful.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0073 }

“I reckon you are referring to being made to go to sleep having had no dinner,” he stated with contempt, “yet that is not terrible. Naturally, I dislike it, but having been put to bed so frequently since my arrival here, I am becoming accustomed to it. Furthermore, you do not economize by denying me dinner, because I invariably consume double the amount when I eat breakfast.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0074 }

“I am not referring to your being ordered to bed. I am referring to the reality that you uttered an untruth today. And, Robin,” . . . Nell bent forward across the footboard of the bed and wagged her finger with solemnity at the transgressor . . . “when a boy speaks what is not genuine, it is nearly the most terrible fate that could befall him . . . nearly the absolute worst. Thus you realize Thirza spoke the truth to you.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0075 }

“However, I assumed that the bad thing would prove thrilling,” Robin objected, feeling hurt.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0076 }

“You cannot hold Thirza responsible for your assumptions. Unfortunate events are not consistently thrilling. In many cases, they are simply unpleasant and senseless.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0077 }

“Though it was mighty amusing watching Thirza and yourself gazing into the well,” Robin remarked, clasping his knees.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0078 }

Nell maintained a serious expression until reaching the lower floor, whereupon she sank onto the couch in the sitting room and giggled to the point of hurting her sides.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0079 }

“I’d like it if you would share the joke with me,” Thirza remarked, her tone somewhat stern. “Not much has happened today that I found amusing.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0080 }

“When you hear this, you’ll laugh,” Nell assured her. Indeed, Thirza laughed, demonstrating the extent to which her education had progressed following the adoption of Nell. Nevertheless, a sigh escaped her right after.
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0081 }

“Although a minister was once heard by me saying it to a child, I guess I ought not to have said that to him. He angered me to such a degree, however. It occurred on the evening when you attended the Delford concert, as I was getting him ready for sleep. His claim was that he failed to perceive any benefit in praying before growing large enough for God to consider him somewhat important. What we will do with that child is unknown to me, Nell. His equal has never been seen by me. Discouragement is completely overwhelming me.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0082 }

“Oh, do not speak like that, Thirza. Recall the terrible state I was in upon my arrival.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0083 }

“Nell, badness was never in you . . . never. Having come to understand actual wickedness, I recognize that now. Admittedly, you constantly found yourself in dreadful trouble, yet your intentions were perpetually noble. Robin simply possesses a genuine affection for being evil.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0084 }

“Oh, no, I doubt he is truly malicious,” Nell urged. “It is merely devilment. Besides, life in this place is somewhat dull for him, as you are aware. Lacking any male companions for recreation, his brain requires an outlet for its energy. Lucy’s extreme rigidity and decorum prevent her from being an adequate companion for a young man. Thirza, my genuine opinion is that sending them to school would be preferable.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0085 }

“No,” Thirza declared with determination, “it was my father's constant view that until a child reached seven years of age, they ought not to be confined within school walls, a sentiment Mr. Wace echoes. While the twins may receive some instruction in the home, they will under no circumstances attend school before turning seven.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0086 }

“Well, we shall have to attempt to improve Robin in our own house instead,” Nell remarked in a bright manner. “Despite every one of his shortcomings, he truly is a sweet young boy. Loving him is something I am unable to avoid. Thirza, expressing this might be terrible, yet truthfully, Robin appeals to me more than Lucy, even though she is so well-behaved.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0087 }

“I admit that I feel somewhat that way as well,” Thirza acknowledged, “and it is unjust, because Lucy causes no difficulty whatsoever. A finer child could not exist, and her presence in the home is scarcely noticeable.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0088 }

“Lucy possesses too much goodness,” Nell remarked. “Even without anyone around to direct her actions, her behavior would remain equally flawless. Because her upbringing was complete from the moment she was born, she has no requirement for us; and my belief is,” Nell ended, striking upon a crucial reality, “that those who require us are the ones who always receive our deepest affection. Our help is desperately required by Robin.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0089 }

“He definitely requires something,” concurred Thirza. “A thorough thrashing is what Agatha Sowerby would claim he needed.”
{: #nw-v02-c10-p0090 }
